claims.claim: Gregory Thaumaturgus (c. 213–c. 270); bishop of Neocaesarea; revered name gathering spuria.
Sermon on All Saints transmitted under his name (martyrs' feast; Christ despoiling Hades).
SCOPE: opening through Christ despoiling Hades.
Gregory Thaumaturgus, also known as Gregory of Neocaesarea, was a Christian bishop of the 3rd century who lived from approximately 213 to 270 AD.
He was born in Neocaesarea in Pontus (modern Niksar, Turkey) to a wealthy pagan family.
He studied with Origen at Caesarea in Palestine for about five years before returning to his native city.
He became bishop of Neocaesarea after being sought out by Phaedimus, bishop of Amasea, who ordained him even though Gregory initially tried to hide from this responsibility.
During the Decian persecution (250–251), Gregory and his community withdrew into the mountains, and after peace was restored he instituted liturgical celebrations honoring the Decian martyrs.
The work 'On All the Saints' is attributed to Gregory Thaumaturgus, though its authenticity is disputed and marked as spurious by some sources.
The sermon was delivered on the feast of All Saints, which was a solemnity among the festivals of the church and attracted a crowded gathering of spectators.
The sermon was delivered at the request of 'the Father' and with the support of the Church, to an assembly of believers gathered for the festival.
The occasion of the sermon was the celebration of the martyrs and all saints, focusing on their victory over death and the devil through martyrdom.
The work survives as a published discourse that was included in collections of the Ante-Nicene Fathers, specifically in volume VI, and was published by Joannes Aloysius Mingarelli in Bologna in 1770.
The feast of All Saints was very ancient in the Oriental churches and was assigned to the Octave of Pentecost.
Gregory was a champion of orthodoxy in the 3rd-century Trinitarian controversy and participated in the Council of Antioch around 264-265 AD that condemned Paul of Samosata.
